articles.title: Ex-partner of powerful far-right Latin American political operator receives asylum in Mexico
articles.author: Pablo Meriguet
articles.content_excerpt: Several weeks ago, Latin America listened intently to the story of a Bolivian woman who had been shot on August 17 and, from a hospital, accused her ex-partner of ordering the hit job. Despite the sordid nature of the story, the news made the front pages of several news outlets because the person making the accusation was Nadia Beller, the ex-partner of Fernando Cerimedo. Cerimedo gained political notoriety in the region as one of the most influential political operatives of the far right in Latin America. Cerimedo was involved in several campaigns supporting far-right candidates who went on to become presidents: Jair Bolsonaro in Brazil, Javier Milei in Argentina, and Nasry Asfura in Honduras. articles.title: Air quality in Delhi at record low due to Diwali festivities, residents demand measures to protect health
articles.author: Abdul Rahman
articles.content_excerpt: India’s capital, Delhi, witnessed a massive deterioration in its air quality over the weekend, making its air unsuitable for human living and a potential public health hazard after the large-scale lighting of firecrackers during Diwali festivities. Delhi was clouded in thick smoke on Sunday and Monday, with various places recording zero visibility with no prospects of improvement in the situation in the coming days. According to India’s Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), during the festivities over the weekend and on Monday, various places in Delhi recorded an Air Quality Index (AQI) of over 400. articles.title: From Ranked-Choice Voting to Dumping Electoral College: Rob Richie on Election Reform Movement
articles.content_excerpt: Alaska is the only Senate race yet to be called. Democratic challenger Mary Peltola is narrowly leading Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan with about 86% of votes counted. Alaska uses ranked-choice voting, a system where voters choose not only their top candidate, but can also indicate an order of preference for remaining candidates on the ballot. If no candidate wins a majority as the top choice, then second-choice votes are added to the totals and so on until there is a winner. articles.title: Farmers in India call for another national mobilization
articles.author: Abdul Rahman
articles.content_excerpt: Farmers unions in India, under the banner of the Samyukta Kisan Morcha (SKM), have called for a nationwide mobilization to protest the attempt to open the country’s agricultural market for foreign competition without addressing the problems they’ve been facing for years. The protests will mark the sixth anniversary of the 2020-21 protests, in which thousands of farmers had camped on the borders of the capital, New Delhi, for months, forcing the government to withdraw farm laws and promise to address other agricultural issues.
